ruling.opinion:
All four counts are adopted with modifications. Three verified facts organize the ruling.

First, the trailing bare-ID line — the proposal's signature guarantee — is illegal under the suite's own normative text (SPECIFICATION.md:347) and rejected by every strict decoder, while libc4 silently corrupts any chain (parser.cpp:278). Those CONFIRMED fatal findings defeat Count 2 as drafted; the case file's claim that the shape is existing grammar is false at the trailing position. But the same record proves the suite already emits exactly this shape: every c4 diff file, and — decisively — every journal append (journal.go:69 writes entry line plus bare-ID boundary, so log.c4m always ends in a bare ID no strict decoder can read). C4M-STANDARD.md:648 simultaneously REQUIRES verifying such checkpoints; c4m ships contradictory pinned tests. A freeze cannot preserve a self-contradiction. Reconciliation is forced onto v1.1.0 regardless of this ruling, and only one direction avoids invalidating every existing store's journal: the trailing validator becomes normative and VERIFIED. That erratum, landed in all five implementations with one shared test vector, is the master release gate; behind it, the prosecution's fatal findings dissolve into coordinated-suite work — its own concession. The decoy-boundary objection is answered structurally: the boundary is the base-section ID, never the root, so a crash-scraped boundary fails c4 cat loudly, and the MUST-verify rule makes the final line consumer-checked. Ordered canonical emission is real engineering — the case file's 'sequential is canonical-ordered' was REFUTED — and is pinned on bytes, with buffered implementations conforming.

Second, Count 3's cost is stated, not papered over. The prosecutor's structural-invariant argument is correct: v8's '-s prints nothing but the claim' protected even negligent consumers by construction; v9 protects them by taxonomy. The court trades that narrow crash-path shield (crash timing plus ignored exit codes) for a structural fix on the success path — the founding complaint-3 consumer failed on a SUCCESSFUL run, and the guaranteed final claim line makes the naive scrape correct — and for Joshua's verbatim requirement, which the prosecution's cat -r read-back does not answer: it buffers everything before showing anything. The shield relocates rather than dies: -s -q keeps v8's empty-on-failure contract verbatim and is the blessed capture. The crash investigation's seven mandatory modifications are adopted in full, including SIGPIPE never cancelling a snapshot and streaming kill-crucible modes before freeze.

Third, Count 1's default flip survives the prosecutor's ledger-reopening charge. The license is named: Joshua's verbatim 'It doesn't have to be built in to the record as nils' — under content-default, every saved default record has nils built in. New evidence the original rejection never saw: every sibling scanner is full-native with no content mode, and full-default makes the front-door -q ID equal the journaled snapshot ID. The silent-trap objection fails safe — drift yields false-different, never false-same. The permanent 2026-07-09 projection decision is untouched. Against the advocate, -s -m c stays refused: a claim-shaped final line that is not the journaled claim rebuilds complaint 3's geometry; the cat -r composition already yields a durable content ID.

Count 4: -c stays trust-only — null-ID-implies-filter would convert a partial scan's recorded ignorance into a silent filter — and the dormant scan.WithGuide is deleted. tail -1 becomes documented, exit-conditioned contract in id(1), never a SCRIPTING recipe: pipeline substitution masks c4's exit, so -q remains THE scripted form. The help/man/changelog re-sweep, the libc4 gate, the loader unification, and the unreadable-directory exit-2 fix all gate the coordinated v1.1.0 release.

arguments: Null semantics are currently corrupted on the design's own terms. v8-as-built manufactures nulls two ways (case-v9.md:30-33): genuine ignorance AND deliberate projection — scan/generator.go:805-813 writes null mode/timestamp into emitted records in ModeContent, and cmd/c4/id.go:421-432 does the same for single files. A null in a saved record is therefore unfalsifiable: no artifact can tell 'unknown at scan time' from 'known and discarded'. This collides head-on with 'Verification over assertion — claims must be recomputable' and 'Partial knowledge is a valid state' (case-v9.md:174-175; workspace design philosophy). Count 1 makes every null mean exactly one thing, which makes every record maximally falsifiable.

Projection is information-monotone only in one direction, and v7 doctrine already picked that direction: '-m projects downward only' (surface-v7.md:121-122). Full→content is computable forever from the saved description; content→full is gone forever — the scanner paid the stat() and then threw the answer away. `c4 id dir > save.c4m` should carry maximum knowledge; today it deliberately destroys knowledge the walk already held. Generation-side projection contradicts the design's own projection doctrine; eval-side projection IS that doctrine.

The projection is cheap at eval time, so nothing is bought by doing it at generation: a directory's ID is the ID of its one-level canonical listing TEXT (surface-v7.md:86-90), so computing content-form IDs from a full manifest means projecting nulls into small listing text and rehashing that text — no byte rehash of any file (case-v9.md:76-78). The cost argument for generation-side projection is zero.

Coherence — one ID at the front door: with full as the default level, `c4 id -q dir` equals the `-s` snapshot ID on an unchanged tree (case-v9.md:85-87). Under v8, the identical tree has two different casual identities depending on whether you happened to store — precisely the confusion family of founding complaints 1 and 3 (brief.md:109-122): the ID captured casually is not the ID that recovers. The brief's design question is the snapshot–store–restore loop (brief.md:22-39); the recovery handle should be the default answer at the front door.

It dissolves a taught-error wart: id.go:38-40 hard-errors on `-s` + `-m` ('snapshots are always full detail'). Under Count 1 storage is always full and `-m` is a view, so the conflict evaporates instead of being documented — fewest concepts, fully load-bearing.
Zero library churn: scan.ModeContent may remain in the library (case-v9.md:82-83); only the CLI moves the projection to evaluation. Siblings are untouched by this count.
subquestion_answers: `-s -m c`: ALLOW it, and pin: the stream is the content-level VIEW of the one full-fidelity scan; the final bare line is the root ID AT THE STREAMED LEVEL, so the chain stays internally valid; the print barrier attaches to that final line regardless (it prints only after the full snapshot is durable and journaled); the snapshot ID stays on stderr (`stored:`) and in the journal. This is safe with ZERO new mechanism because `-s` already stores BOTH full-form and content-form listings for every directory, root included (surface-v7.md:75-77; draft-v7 §2) — so the printed content root ID resolves in the store and 'printed ⇒ you can get it back' holds for both kinds. Bonus contract line this makes possible: `CID=$(c4 id -s -q -m c dir/)` — a DURABLE cross-machine content ID in one command, new power arriving purely as a consequence of existing design.

Machine-contract cost: accept it explicitly — the cross-machine line becomes `CID=$(c4 id -q -m c dir/)` (case-v9.md:88-90). One flag, self-documenting, and 'compare like with like, scanned alike' was always the doctrine (surface-v7.md:27): no default ever exempted both sides from matching -S and exclusion choices, so both sides typing `-m c` is symmetric, not a regression.

counts.position: ADOPT — streaming chain output as the default shape
arguments: Joshua's verbatim requirement is a hard functional gap, not taste: buffered-only output 'blocks a large class of command-line utilities (finding an id on a very large tree, incremental saving, grep interaction)' (case-v9.md:56-62). v8-as-built is fully buffered: GenerateFromPath returns a complete manifest, THEN outputManifest encodes it (id.go:151-162, 321-341, 729-735); nothing prints until the scan completes (case-v9.md:29). On a terabyte media tree that is minutes-to-hours of silence on stdout.

'Partial data is data' is a founding pin, and v8 violates it on output: a killed v8 scan leaves NOTHING; a killed streaming scan leaves a valid partial c4m description (case-v9.md:104-105) — exactly the 'materialize 9 of 10, reference the 10th' degradation the philosophy demands (case-v9.md:174-175). Joshua names this verbatim: 'Forcing full computation before progress violates that philosophy when that computation is long' (case-v9.md:64-67).

Zero new grammar — the frozen format already contains the answer (case-v9.md:97-98). Patch chains, null fields, and bare-ID boundary lines are EXISTING frozen grammar (brief.md:45-51; case-v9.md:165-167). Directory lines stream with null ID/size — genuine ignorance at that instant, exactly Count 1's null semantics; the trailing refinement section and bare root-ID validator are ordinary chain mechanics already implemented (c4m/chain.go:53-98; trailing bare ID as validator, chain.go:92-94). This is the single purest instance in the whole proposal of 'new power arrives as a consequence of the existing design, not as an addition to it.'

The ecosystem already speaks chains, because the STORE JOURNAL is a chain: <store>/log.c4m is 'an ordinary c4m patch chain' (surface-v7.md:359-361). Concretely: Go c4m owns DecodePatchChain (chain.go:23); c4sh links that library (c4sh/go.mod:6, c4 v1.0.16); c4py parses bare-ID block links (c4py/src/c4py/decoder.py:114-141); c4ts handles patch boundaries (c4ts/packages/core/src/decoder.ts:384-435); c4m-swift treats bare IDs as checkpoints/block links (Sources/C4M/Decoder.swift:25-79); vscode-c4m's TextMate grammar simply leaves a bare-ID line unstyled — a highlighter has no failure mode (syntaxes/c4m.tmLanguage.json). The sole real gap is libc4 (src/c4m/parser.cpp:278 skips boundaries, 'not yet supported') — a bounded pre-release fix, not an architectural objection, and note libc4 already cannot correctly read the journal today, so the gap predates v9.

Determinism is already solved machinery, not a new invariant: the parallel walk guarantees byte-identical output at any concurrency by stitching children back in post-sort order (generator.go:180-181), and WithEntryStream exists with the caveat precisely named (generator.go:198-216). Ordered emission with bounded lookahead is engineering INSIDE an existing invariant.

Memory: v8 holds the entire manifest of a 10M-entry tree in RAM before a single byte prints. Streaming bounds working memory; the refinement patch retains only directory lines — a vanishing fraction of entries.

The founding wrong-ID trap dies the other way: the LAST line of the stream is always the root ID (case-v9.md:105-106), so the scrape a cold consumer will actually write — `tail -1` — becomes CORRECT. The trap existed because the root ID appeared nowhere in its own listing (case-v9.md:36-41); v9 puts it in the one place every shell idiom looks.
subquestion_answers: Chain shape: ONE trailing refinement patch. The stream is: entries in canonical DFS order (directory lines with null ID/size) — then the bare ID of the streamed base text (the block-link form c4py/decoder.py:141 and Decoder.swift:79 already parse; cheap, it hashes bytes already emitted) — then the refinement section filling directory IDs/sizes — then the bare root ID as the trailing validator (chain.go:92-94). Per-directory patches multiply sections for no consumer benefit and are rejected.

-e under streaming: -e IMPLIES BUFFERED, documented in FLAGS. Alignment needs global column widths; -e is the human view and was never the machine form, so byte-purity and streaming semantics of the data shape are unharmed.

`c4 id file.c4m` normalization: YES, emits flat resolved canonical text — chains already resolve on parse (id.go:260-267 and the loadManifest path), so `c4 id f.c4m` is the sanctioned flattener and the round-trip `c4 id dir > f.c4m; c4 id f.c4m` is total.

Ordered emission: canonical DFS order out, parallel hashing underneath, emission blocking on next-in-order with a BOUNDED lookahead window; when the window fills, workers block (backpressure) — a slow subtree can never balloon memory. Determinism is inherited from the existing post-sort stitching invariant (generator.go:180-181); WithEntryStream's discovery-order behavior (generator.go:203-207) is the named engineering item, not an unknown.

Gating: streaming is UNCONDITIONAL — no flag, no isatty. isatty-dependent DATA is banned outright (case-v9.md:118-120; surface-v7 permits isatty only for stderr narration), and one output shape everywhere is fewest-concepts: the same bytes to a terminal, a pipe, and a file.

Consumer compatibility: chain-shaped `c4 id` output is a release gate for libc4 (fix parser.cpp to resolve, not skip, boundaries) and a doc sweep elsewhere; every other consumer demonstrably parses chains today (citations above), because the journal made chains a first-class artifact in v7.

counts.position: ADOPT — `-s` streams the listing; the claim is the final line (reversing v8's '-s implies -q')
arguments: It restores the founding ergonomic Joshua states verbatim: 'c4 id -s dir outputs c4m — it's pipeable, and using it is much like ls -l… maybe not at the expense of existing ergonomics' (case-v9.md:49-53). Under v8-as-built (`-s` implies `-q`, id.go:37-42; draft-v8.md:158-161), the most natural workflow — snapshot AND see/pipe what was captured — costs either a SECOND full scan or a store read-back (`c4 cat -r "$SNAP"`, case-v9.md:26-27). The design punishes its own primary loop with doubled cost on exactly the large trees where the loop matters. One command should scan once, store, and pipe the listing — composition over configuration.

The division of labor is already correct in the flag set: -q is the byte-pure scripted form (one line, nothing else — unchanged machine contract), so bare -s serving humans and pipes costs machines nothing. v8 optimized the default for the script at the expense of the human when the script already had its dedicated spelling. Ergonomics are adoption: `id -s` is the verb users run per-prompt, all day.

The print barrier is preserved, not weakened, where it matters: the FINAL bare root-ID line prints only after content is durable and the journal appended (case-v9.md:127-131). Printed-claim semantics get pinned crisply: streamed entry lines are description, never claims; only the final bare ID line and -q lines carry 'printed ⇒ durable ⇒ recoverable' (case-v9.md:137-139). This is not new doctrine — the contract has ALWAYS said 'an ID scraped out of entry text is some entry's' and 'The printed text is entries, not the identity' (surface-v7.md:31, 68-69); without -s, printed entry IDs were never claims (case-v9.md:141-144). v9 makes the description/claim distinction uniform across all modes instead of mode-dependent.

Founding complaint 3 dies structurally rather than by silence: v8 fenced the trap by printing nothing; v9 removes the trap by making the root ID the guaranteed final stdout line, so the obvious scrape (`tail -1`) is the correct one (case-v9.md:132-135). A trap you cannot fall into by doing the obvious thing is safer than a trap fenced by a convention the cold user must first learn. And a killed -s stream self-evidently carries no claim: the final line is simply absent.
subquestion_answers: Does a partial stream mislead? Pin one sentence at id(1) DURABILITY and in the SCRIPTING block: 'streamed entry lines are description, never claims; only the final bare ID line (and every -q line) prints after durability.' This is the same doc mechanism that carries every other durability sentence on the surface (surface-v7.md:149-158). Child IDs visible before a crash are exactly as trustworthy as they were under plain `c4 id` — which is to say, description, recomputable, never claims (the defense the case file itself states, case-v9.md:141-144).

Multi-path `-s a b c`: -q keeps the existing contract verbatim — one bare line per SUCCEEDED path, pairing valid only on exit 0, scripts snapshot one path per invocation (surface-v7.md:46-48, already the sanctioned rule). Non-q multi-path emits complete per-path chains in argument order, each closed by its own bare root-ID claim line; the exit-pairing rule survives unchanged because it was only ever guaranteed under -q/exit-0. Nothing new to invent.

counts.position: ADOPT — subsidiary surface: -c trust-only; tail -1 sanctioned; -s -q blessed; full doc re-sweep
arguments: -c stays TRUST-ONLY (the v8 status quo, draft-v8.md Amendment 1). Overloading it with SCOPE silently breaks stale-guide re-scans — new files would VANISH from the description instead of being hashed (case-v9.md:151-153), a safe-by-default violation of the worst kind: silent data omission in a tool whose product is claims about completeness. 'Guide entries with null IDs imply filter' is implicit magic and condemned on sight. Fewest concepts: one flag, one meaning — the reuse guide with the racy rule. If the retired filter workflow ever earns its way back, it arrives as an explicit flag later — capability added from outside, when demanded.

Contract migration, pinned: (a) `SNAP=$(c4 id -s -q dir/)` is the blessed capture form (the -q line keeps the v8 one-line guarantee verbatim); (b) `tail -1` is SANCTIONED as contract — 'the last stdout line of any successful non-q id invocation is the root ID' — because sanctioning converts the scrape every shell user will write anyway into a guarantee, while mere tolerance leaves it folklore that a future change could break; (c) `CID=$(c4 id -q -m c dir/)` is the cross-machine content line, and `CID=$(c4 id -s -q -m c dir/)` its durable twin (sound at zero mechanism because both listing forms are already stored per surface-v7.md:75-77).

Timing makes the sweep cheap and mandatory: v8 is merged and UNRELEASED, and the machine contract freezes at v1.1.0 (case-v9.md:9-16, 168-171) — this is definitionally the last cheap moment. The help/man re-sweep is bounded, mechanical, and has zero installed-base migration debt: the exact lines are locatable now (help.go:40-41 SNAP/CID recipes, help.go:219-229 flag text and examples, plus the changelog).
subquestion_answers: SCRIPTING block replacement text (the lines that change): 'SNAP=$(c4 id -s -q dir/)  THE snapshot ID: one line, nothing else' ; 'CID=$(c4 id -q -m c dir/)  THE content ID — machine/clock/umask-independent, compare like with like' ; 'c4 id -s dir/ | tail -1  the root ID is always the final line of the stream (sanctioned)' ; plus the final-line claim-semantics sentence from Count 3.

Changelog/help/man: full re-sweep required and in scope for the ruling — every occurrence of 'content (default)', '-s implies -q', and the -s/-m conflict text (help.go:219-221) changes; the identity block's 'default level' sentence (surface-v7 lineage, help.go:19-28 analog) is rewritten to full-default with -m as downward projection.

advocate.strongest_opposing_argument: The flatten-rule / default-shape objection, at full strength: Counts 1+2 together change what `c4 id dir` means at the deepest layer. Today the default output is flat canonical text whose BYTES hash to the ID it denotes — the flatten rule, 'a description's canonical-text ID equals its root ID at its own knowledge level' (draft-v7 §1) — at a machine-independent level, per D1's permanent-flavored rationale that 'THE identity should be machine/clock/umask-independent by default' (case-v9.md:42-46). Under v9 the default becomes a CHAIN whose raw bytes do NOT hash to the final root ID, at a machine-DEPENDENT level. Two invariants weaken simultaneously and permanently (the contract freezes at v1.1.0): every consumer that hashes or naively parses raw `c4 id` output breaks — and one shipping implementation, libc4, would TODAY silently mis-resolve a chain-shaped file into a wrong manifest (parser.cpp:278 skips boundaries and would flatten refinement entries into the base); and the cold T3 user comparing two checkouts across machines now gets a false 'different' from the bare command, with no diagnostic, forever. The advocate's answer: (i) resolution-closure is already the ecosystem norm — the journal is a chain (surface-v7.md:359-361) and .c4m arguments 'resolve to final state' on parse in every verb (surface-v7.md:115-116) — so the replacement invariant is one sentence ('the canonical text of a description's RESOLUTION hashes to its root ID; c4 id f.c4m emits that text'), and the libc4 fix is a hard, cheap release gate for a defect that predates v9 (libc4 cannot read the journal correctly today either); (ii) like-with-like was always mandatory (surface-v7.md:27 — no default ever exempted matching -S and exclusions), T3 keeps a one-flag self-documenting answer, and the default now answers the more frequent and more dangerous question — the recovery identity — with ONE ID at the front door instead of two.
concessions: libc4 is a hard release gate: src/c4m/parser.cpp:278 skips bare-ID boundaries ('not yet supported'), so chain-shaped default output would today be silently mis-resolved into a wrong manifest by one shipping implementation. Chain resolution must land in libc4 before v1.1.0 ships; I concede v9 turns a latent gap into a live one.

The flatten rule genuinely weakens from a one-step invariant ('the bytes you see hash to the ID') to a resolution-level one ('the resolved canonical text hashes to the ID'). That is a real loss of a beautiful sentence, and every surface site stating it must be found and restated.

Cross-machine content comparison now costs an explicit `-m c`, T3's blessed recipe changes, and some cold user will compare full-level IDs across machines and get a false negative before reading the identity block. Every doc line saying 'content is the default' (help.go:221 among others) must be re-swept; a missed one is a live contradiction in frozen contract text.

v8's structural guarantee under -s — nothing on stdout until the claim — was strictly STRONGER than v9's doc-pinned final-line rule: a mid-stream kill under v9 shows child IDs on stdout that may not be durable in the store, and the defense is a documentation sentence, not a mechanism.

Canonical-order streaming emission with bounded lookahead does not exist yet: WithEntryStream emits discovery order under the parallel walk (generator.go:203-207). This is new engineering plus memory-bound and determinism testing on the v1.1.0 critical path; I claim it extends an existing invariant (generator.go:180-181), but it is unbuilt.

-e implies buffered is a documented asymmetry: the ergonomic view loses every streaming benefit, and users who habitually pass -e get v8-style latency without an explanation unless the doc line lands well.

Under my proposed `-s -m c` resolution, the final claim line is the CONTENT root ID, not the snapshot ID — the recovery handle lives on stderr and in the journal for that invocation. Sound (both listing forms are stored), but it is a teaching burden and the one place where 'the final line is the ID you want' needs a qualifier.

counts.position: REJECT AS PROPOSED — adopt only the internal mechanism (eval-side projection), keep content as the default view and default -q identity. Defend D1's default.
arguments: The default-full listing/ID is a reopened, still-standing ledger rejection. round-1/ledger.json entry 29: 'all prior REJECTED entries stand (stat-bearing default IDs; ...)' with 'no candidate produced a named new-context license to reopen any of them.' Count 1's 'Default listing level = FULL' makes `c4 id -q dir/` print a stat-bearing (mtime-carrying) ID by default — precisely the rejected class. No named new context reopens it: Joshua's verbatim challenge (case-v9.md:47-67) asks for eval-side nulls, streaming, and -s ergonomics; it never asks to change the default identity level. The assistant's synthesis smuggled the default flip in as a 'consequence' when it is separable.

Eval-side projection and content-default are orthogonal. The scanner can capture full knowledge and project at output while CONTENT remains the default printed view and -q identity — byte-identical CLI output to v8-as-built (scan.ModeContent generates the same nulls the projector would emit; cmd/c4/id.go:421-433). Joshua's literal request — 'The nil metadata fields can simply be on the eval side not on the generation side' — is fully satisfied without touching D1's default. The prosecution adopts the mechanism and prosecutes only the default flip riding on it.

D1's rationale is load-bearing product surface, not taste: 'THE identity should be machine/clock/umask-independent by default' (case-v9.md:43-46). Brief task T3 (brief.md:150-153) demands one identifier answering 'byte-identical content?' by string equality, and the blessed recipe is the zero-flag front door: 'CID=$(c4 id -q dir/) THE content ID' (surface-v7.md:33). Under Count 1 the same bytes checked out on two machines produce UNEQUAL default IDs (mtimes differ), a false-negative on the commonest cross-machine question, and the machine-contract line grows a flag (`-m c`) that every cold consumer must know to omit wrongness — the resolver-lab class of consumer (brief.md founding complaint 3) will not know it.

The claimed 'coherence win' — `c4 id -q dir` equals the `-s` snapshot ID — is a trap dressed as a guarantee: it holds only 'on an unchanged tree' (case-v9.md:85-87). Any mtime drift (a build, an editor save, a checkout) between the two invocations silently breaks the equality. A coherence property that fails silently under ordinary filesystem noise teaches consumers a false invariant; v8's two-named-IDs story (content ID = comparison handle, snapshot ID = recovery handle, surface-v7.md:19-28) never pretends they coincide.

The purity claim 'nulls mean ignorance only' cannot actually be delivered by Count 1: any PRINTED `-m c` document still contains deliberately projected nulls, whatever the scanner captured internally. Null semantics are honestly stated per-form under v8 already — full-form nulls are ignorance; a content-form document is definitionally a projection, and per the permanent 2026-07-09 decision the projection travels out of band and an ID never self-describes it (brief.md:52-58). Count 1 buys internal cleanliness, zero observable consumer behavior — a cost-free adoption only if the default is left alone.
proposed_modifications: ADOPT eval-side projection as library/CLI mechanism: scanner captures full fidelity; `-m c` becomes a projection applied at output/identity time (content directory IDs computed from projected listing text — cheap, no byte rehash; file content IDs are byte hashes and identical in either mode).
KEEP content as the default `c4 id` listing level and default `-q` identity. The machine-contract SCRIPTING lines do not change: `CID=$(c4 id -q dir/)`.

Dissolve the `-s`/`-m` conflict only in one direction: `-s` stores full (unchanged); a `-s -m c` combination remains REFUSED — printing an ID-bearing content view on the same stdout as (or instead of) a claimed full snapshot ID puts two unequal root identities in one command's output, the wrong-ID trap in one invocation (answers the case's own sub-question, case-v9.md:88-89).
One scan may now serve both IDs (project after full capture) — document `c4 id -q dir/` and `c4 id -q -m f dir/` as views of one read; this is the entire ergonomic content of Count 1 worth keeping.
subquestion_answers: Should `-s -m c` print a content view while claiming a full snapshot ID? NO — refuse, as v8 does. Two root identities of the same tree on one stdout, only one of which is the claim, is founding complaint 3's geometry reconstructed deliberately.

counts.position: REJECT chain-shaped output as THE DEFAULT shape of `c4 id`. If the court adopts any streaming, adopt only with the modifications below; the burden of suite-wide consumer readiness is unmet today.
arguments: A shipped implementation silently mis-parses chains TODAY: libc4/src/c4m/parser.cpp:278-279 — 'Skip bare C4 ID lines (patch boundaries -- not yet supported in C++ impl)'. Feed it a chain-shaped `c4 id dir > f.c4m` and it drops the boundaries, concatenating the null-ID base section and the refinement section into one flat manifest with duplicate paths and null directory IDs — no error, wrong data. Making the flagship verb's DEFAULT stdout a shape one suite member silently corrupts, then freezing that default in v1.1.0 (case-v9.md:168-171), is a coordinated-release violation manufactured at design time. (c4py, c4ts, c4m-swift do resolve chains — c4ts/packages/core/src/decoder.ts:384-393, c4m-swift Decoder.swift:25-26 — but 'most consumers cope' is not the standard for a frozen default.)

The chain shape necessarily places at least TWO bare 90-char ID lines on stdout where v8's default places ZERO. Sections must be separated by a bare-ID boundary line (c4m/chain.go:53-76: a bare ID flushes the current section; entries appended without a boundary would be one section with duplicate paths). So the stream is [base entries][bare boundary ID][patch entries][bare root ID] — and the boundary ID is NOT the identity. The founding complaint (brief.md complaint 3) was a consumer scraping DEFAULT output and shipping a wrong ID; v9's default output now contains a syntactically perfect decoy. v8's default listing contains no bare IDs at all — the root ID appears nowhere in its own listing (case-v9.md:38-41) — which is why v8 routed identity through -q/-s instead of making scraping 'easier'.

`tail -1` is unsound on truncated captures. A stream cut by kill, SIGPIPE, or a dropped SSH channel can end exactly at the boundary bare-ID line; `tail -1` then yields a valid-looking, wrong ID. Only exit-code discipline saves the consumer — and the documented complaint-3 population (regex-scrapers who probed membership by side effects) is defined by not having that discipline. v8's `-q`/`-s` fails STRUCTURALLY safe: killed before the print barrier, stdout is empty, and an empty capture cannot be mistaken for an ID (cmd/c4/id.go:534-537: the ID is reported only after syncStore + journalClaim).

The determinism pin is not free. 'Byte-identical output at any concurrency' (case-v9.md:172; project design philosophy) requires ordered emission the codebase does not have: scan.WithEntryStream is documented as 'discovery order produced by the worker pool, which is non-deterministic across runs; pair with WithMaxConcurrency(1) for a deterministic order' (scan/generator.go:203-207). Canonical-order emission under the parallel walk needs blocking-on-next-in-order plus a bounded lookahead; a slow first subtree stalls emission while workers fill the bound, degenerating toward buffering-with-extra-machinery. The proposal files this as a 'sub-question' (case-v9.md:113-117); it is the entire engineering cost, spent to make the machine-facing default shape worse so the human-facing latency is better.

It inverts the stdout/stderr doctrine. The brief makes machines the primary stdout audience ('what the verbs print is the API', brief.md complaint 3; LLM agents first-class, brief.md:136-137), and humans already have a live progress channel: 'one live line on a terminal, replaced at completion by one summary line' on stderr (surface-v7.md:82-84). Streaming's beneficiaries — eyeballs, grep-while-waiting, head — are the narration audience; its cost — a two-section shape every parser must resolve, flag-dependent shape under -e (alignment needs global widths, case-v9.md:108-110) — lands entirely on the data audience.

The ergonomic gains are narrower than claimed. Total scan time is unchanged — streaming moves latency-to-first-line only; 'finding an id on a very large tree' is better served by scanning the subpath directly (`c4 id dir/sub`); and grep over the full listing needs the full walk regardless. The genuinely new powers are early pipe termination (head) and a killed scan leaving a usable partial file-level description — real, but they do not require being the DEFAULT.
proposed_modifications: If adopted at all: `-e` is pinned as buffered, flat, canonical output — the v8 shape — so one EXISTING flag recovers the flat contract (no budget spent; -e already exists, cmd/c4/id.go:27).

`c4 id file.c4m` normalization emits FLAT text, always: chains are a transport/transcript shape of a live scan; flat canonical text remains the one stored and normalized form (storeManifestSelf stores flat records, cmd/c4/id.go:547-581 — stdout must not diverge in kind from the store's artifacts).

The boundary bare-ID line is pinned (which ID it is, stated in the grammar-usage doc) and documented in id(1) and the SCRIPTING block as never-the-identity; the contract sentence is 'the LAST line of a COMPLETE (exit-0) stream is the root ID' — completeness and exit code named in the same sentence.

v1.1.0 release-gates on chain-resolution parity landing in libc4 (parser.cpp:278 TODO closed) plus a resolution-parity test vector shared across c4py/c4ts/c4m-swift/libc4 — RELEASE.md suite discipline applied before the default changes shape.

Ordered emission pinned on BYTES, not timing: byte-identical at any concurrency, with the bounded-lookahead rule stated; a fully buffered implementation is a conforming implementation of the streaming contract.
subquestion_answers: Chain shape: one trailing refinement patch, never per-directory patches — per-directory patches multiply boundary bare-ID decoys and section count without bounding memory better.

-e under streaming: -e implies buffered flat (alignment needs global column widths; a flag silently changing stdout's grammatical shape is acceptable only if the shape it selects is the old canonical one).
`c4 id file.c4m` emits flat text: yes, unconditionally.

Streaming gating: never isatty-gated (byte-purity pin, case-v9.md:118-120 concedes this); if not default, there is no flag budget left (--force, --verify spent per draft-v8.md:81-84) — which is itself an argument that the change is premature for v1.1.0.
Consumer compatibility: NOT satisfied today — libc4 silently mis-parses (parser.cpp:278-279); adoption requires the release gate above.

counts.position: REJECT — defend v8's '-s implies -q'. The print barrier's 'nothing printed until claimed' is a structural invariant; Count 3 trades it for a documentation convention.
arguments: v8's claim rule is structural: the claiming command's stdout IS the claim — 'ONE bare line — THE snapshot ID — after content is durable and the journal appended' (case-v9.md:23-27; help.go:40 'THE snapshot ID: one line, nothing else'; enforced in code at cmd/c4/id.go:530-537, syncStore + journalClaim before report). Count 3 replaces this with a line taxonomy a reader must learn from docs: entry lines are description, the mid-chain boundary bare ID is not a claim, only the FINAL bare ID line carries printed⇒durable (case-v9.md:135-139). The brief's first-class users are cold LLM agents driving from --help (brief.md:136-137); conventions distinguishing look-alike lines are precisely what that population gets wrong, and the round-1 sims showed the SCRIPTING block is read at skim depth (draft-v7.md:23-24).

It falsifies a load-bearing surface sentence as written. 'A printed ID never dangles: if it printed, you can get it back' (surface-v7.md:52-53, 157-158) and T1's premise ('the last ID the tool printed', brief.md:141-145) both quantify over EVERYTHING printed. Under streaming -s killed before the barrier, stdout of the claiming command holds child IDs (in entry text) and a boundary bare ID that may name nothing durable. The replacement invariant — 'only bare final-ID lines and -q lines are claims' — is strictly weaker and must be stated with exceptions where v8's is total. The ruling would have to log this as a weakened round-1 invariant; the prosecution says the weakening buys one saved command.

The 'trap dies the other way' defense sanctifies `tail -1`, which is exactly wrong on the failure path: a stream truncated after the boundary bare ID leaves `tail -1` returning a plausible non-claim ID (see Count 2, argument 3). v8's blessed capture `SNAP=$(c4 id -s dir/)` is whole-stdout capture — no scrape, no line selection, empty-on-failure. You cannot improve on a contract whose failure mode is the empty string.

Multi-path -s collapses to opt-in safety. The one-ID-line-per-SUCCEEDED-path pin (surface-v7.md:46-48, 77-80; help.go:55-56) was itself a round-1 repair of complaint-3 misattribution. Count 3 concedes 'the one-line-per-path contract only holds under -q' (case-v9.md:145-147) — i.e., the machine contract survives only behind a flag. That inverts the binding constraint 'Safe by default' (case-v9.md:174): v9 is legible-by-default, safe-by-flag.

The ergonomic loss v8 imposes is one command, not a pipe-and-tee. Joshua's stated fear — needing 'a pipe and tee to a second c4' (case-v9.md:59-61) — is already answered on the v8 surface: `SNAP=$(c4 id -s dir/)` then `c4 cat -r "$SNAP"` returns the full listing from the store with verified reads and zero re-scan (case-v9.md:27-28; surface-v7.md cat(1)). Composition over new surface is the house doctrine; the porcelain-documents-its-composition rule says put that two-liner in the SCRIPTING block, not rebuild the claim channel around it.

Streaming -s also un-fixes complaint 1's shape at the margin: the streamed listing on stdout is a transcript that the store does NOT contain byte-for-byte (the store holds flat per-directory records, cmd/c4/id.go:547-581), inviting consumers to save the stream as 'the c4m' when the canonical recoverable description is the store's — a subtler version of trusting captured text over the store that T1 exists to kill.
proposed_modifications: Keep v8: `-s` implies `-q`; one bare claim line per succeeded path; nothing printed until claimed.

Add to the SCRIPTING block the two-line idiom: `SNAP=$(c4 id -s dir/) && c4 cat -r "$SNAP"` — 'snapshot, then read the listing back verified from the store' — naming it as THE replacement for the old pipeable -s.

If the court nonetheless adopts streaming -s: (i) the claim-rule sentence must be printed in the -s help text itself, not only the SCRIPTING block; (ii) multi-path -s REFUSES without -q (streams from multiple roots may not interleave with claims — refuse rather than document guesswork); (iii) `stored: <ID>` stderr narration is kept so humans have a claim signal independent of line position; (iv) the changelog and machine-contract migration section must state in one line that plain `-s` stdout changed shape between v1.0.x and v1.1.0.
subquestion_answers: Does a partial stream mislead? YES, materially: the mid-chain boundary bare ID is a claim-shaped line that is not a claim; entry-text IDs precede durability. 'Without -s, printed IDs were never claims anyway' does not answer WITH -s, where v8 consumers have been taught that this command's stdout is the claim.
Multi-path `-s a b c`: incoherent under streaming — refuse without -q rather than pin an interleaving grammar (see modification ii).

counts.position: ADOPT v8 status quo — `-c` carries trust only. Reject scope-overloading and null-ID-implies-filter. On contract migration: tail -1 is tolerated only with exit-0 stated in the same sentence; the blessed capture form stays whole-stdout, not a scrape.
arguments: The case names the disqualifying defect itself: overloading -c with scope 'silently breaks stale-guide re-scans (new files would vanish instead of hashing)' (case-v9.md:151-155). A safety-relevant silent omission triggered by an ordinary input (a guide that aged) is the exact class the exclusion ledger condemned — ambient/implicit state silently changing what an ID names (ledger.json entry 21 reasoning; entry 16's condemned-divergence standard).

Guide-entries-with-null-IDs-imply-filter is implicit magic by the case's own label (case-v9.md:154-155) and double-charges one flag with two meanings distinguishable only by data inspection. Amendment 1 deliberately re-pointed -c at trust ('its meaning is now the reuse guide, not a path filter', draft-v8.md:26-28); reviving the retired v1.0.x filter workflow answers no founding complaint and no brief task. Fewest concepts, fully load-bearing: an explicit second flag LATER, if a task ever demands it, is the only clean path — and the flag budget is spent (draft-v8.md:81-84), which is the system telling you the demand is not real yet.

Contract migration: `SNAP=$(c4 id -s dir/)` (v8 form) remains the blessed capture — whole-stdout, single path, empty-on-failure. `tail -1` must never appear in the SCRIPTING block for id: it is sound only on complete exit-0 streams (Count 2, argument 3), and the one place tail -1 is documented today is `c4 log | tail -1` (help.go:372) — a verb whose every line is a complete record, which is why it is safe there and not on a stream. If any streaming count is adopted, the sanctioned scripting form is `-s -q`, the migration note names the -s shape change explicitly, and the v1.1.0 changelog/help sweep (case-v9.md:162-163) is a release gate, not a follow-up.
proposed_modifications: None to v8 for -c. Migration text: bless `SNAP=$(c4 id -s dir/)`; if streaming ships anywhere, bless `SNAP=$(c4 id -s -q dir/)` and tolerate `tail -1` only in a sentence that also requires checking exit 0.
subquestion_answers: -c scope: trust-only (v8 status quo). Filter workflow: dead until a named task revives it with its own explicit flag.
tail -1: tolerated for `c4 log` (structured records), never sanctioned for id streams; the blessed capture is whole-stdout command substitution plus exit check.

prosecutor.strongest_opposing_argument: The proposal's strongest ground is that it derives genuinely new power from frozen primitives alone — the house's own aesthetic test. Flat canonical text structurally cannot stream (a directory line carries bottom-up aggregates), so v8's buffered default hard-codes a violation of a founding pin: 'partial knowledge is a valid state, not an error' becomes 'no knowledge until total knowledge' at the front door, exactly Joshua's complaint that 'forcing full computation before progress violates that philosophy when that computation is long.' The patch chain is already grammar; null directory IDs during the walk are honest ignorance under Count 1's semantics; a killed scan leaves a valid partial description whose file-level IDs are real and immediately reusable as a -c reuse guide (buildReuseMap needs only file entries with real IDs, scan/generator.go:242-267) — so streaming turns every interrupted scan from zero into capital. And the final-line rule attacks the founding wrong-ID trap from the opposite side: the trap existed because the root ID appeared NOWHERE in default output; making it the guaranteed last line of a complete stream gives the naive consumer a correct instinct instead of punishing an inevitable one. That is a coherent, format-native reframe, not a bolt-on — the strongest single reason to take the whole package seriously.
concessions: Eval-side projection as an internal mechanism is strictly better engineering than v8's generation-side ModeContent: one read can serve both identities, scanner knowledge stays maximal, and the -s/-m tension dissolves; I adopt it with the default unchanged — my quarrel is only with the default flip riding on it.

v8's fully buffered bare `c4 id` really does block head/grep early-exit and leaves NOTHING useful behind on kill, whereas a killed chain stream leaves a valid partial description reusable as a -c guide; the 'total time is unchanged' rebuttal does not answer latency-to-first-byte or interrupted-scan capital.

The founding wrong-ID cure never strictly required '-s implies -q'; it requires -q existing plus the SCRIPTING block, which the round-1 doc-only sims showed carries most of the load (draft-v7.md:19-24). v8's one-line -s is belt-and-braces; a court could loosen the braces without reopening complaint 3, provided multi-path -s refuses without -q.

`tail -1` plus an exit-0 check is a sound contract for disciplined scripts; my truncation objection applies only to the undisciplined-consumer population that complaint 3 documents — a real population, but a bounded one.

The libc4 breakage argument is contingent, not principled: if chain-resolution parity lands in libc4 and a shared resolution test vector gates the coordinated v1.1.0 release, Count 2's worst concrete harm dissolves into ordinary suite-release work.

On an unchanged tree, Count 1's coherence property (front-door -q ID == snapshot ID) would genuinely simplify the two-IDs teaching burden that round-1 sims flagged as the surface's hardest concept; I reject it because it fails silently under mtime noise, not because the coherence itself lacks value.

findings.claim: WithEntryStream today guarantees only set-completeness with a mutex-serialized callback; emission order under the default parallel walk is discovery order and is non-deterministic across runs. Ordered canonical emission is NOT provided by any current mode.
findings.evidence: scan/generator.go:199-216 (doc: 'Order is the discovery order produced by the worker pool, which is non-deterministic across runs'); scan/generator.go:401-408 (emit serialized by streamMu); scan/stream_test.go:44-49 (contract tested is set equality only, 'the set of streamed entries == the set of final manifest entries'). Empirical: 40-dir x 40-file tree, 6 scan.Dir runs with WithEntryStream produced 6 distinct emission-order hashes (scratch experiment, go run ./order).

findings.claim: The case file's parenthetical 'sequential mode is canonical-ordered' is false on two axes: sequential emission is readdir-lexical (not files-first natural sort) and directories emit post-order (after children), while canonical flat c4m is pre-order. No current emission order can be piped as canonical flat text.
findings.evidence: Empirical (WithMaxConcurrency(1) on tree {a.txt,f2.txt,f10.txt,sub/...}): emit order 'a.txt, f10.txt, f2.txt, c.txt, d.txt, deeper/, sub/' vs final canonical 'a.txt, f2.txt, f10.txt, sub/, c.txt, deeper/, d.txt'. Code: scan/generator.go:550-634 (children processed in os.ReadDir order), :735 (dir self-entry emitted after children resolve), :209-211 (post-order documented); canonical sort only after walk at generator.go:480 (manifest.SortEntries) and c4m/manifest.go:129-136 (files first, NaturalLess). Stitch-in-source-order at generator.go:697-710 orders only the returned slice, never the stream.

findings.claim: Ordered canonical-DFS emission with parallel hashing is implementable but requires: per-directory canonical pre-sort at readdir (cheap — readdir yields type info), pre-order dir lines with null ID/size (grammar supports), and a reorder buffer gating emission on next-in-canonical-order completion. Worst-case buffering is the wide flat directory: head-of-line blocking behind the slowest early file buffers O(N) entries unbounded, or bounded lookahead K caps memory at O(K + depth) at the price of idling workers. Deep narrow trees are nearly free for the reorder buffer (O(depth)).
findings.evidence: scan/generator.go:636-691 (subdir dispatch is uncoordinated across siblings; non-blocking semaphore acquire means completion order is arbitrary); generator.go:507-534 (dir Size/Timestamp/C4ID resolved only bottom-up after children — so pre-order dir lines MUST be null-ID/null-size, which is exactly the proposal's Count 1 null semantics); c4m grammar already round-trips null size '-' and null ID '-' (c4m/decoder.go:345-352, 483-488; verified empirically in the chain experiment where 'drwxr-xr-x <ts> - sub/ -' parsed and resolved). The reorder-buffer analysis is reasoning from these code facts, not a measurement.

findings.claim: The trailing refinement patch inherently costs O(#dirs) retained memory regardless of tree shape (every directory's refined line must be held until walk completion); for typical trees (files >> dirs) this is a large reduction vs v8's full buffering, but for pathological all-directory trees it equals full buffering. v8 today buffers the entire manifest AND copies it again inside Encode.
findings.evidence: Root/dir IDs are bottom-up aggregates (scan/generator.go:712-734; c4m/manifest.go:105-127 — WriteCanonical hashes only the top-level listing whose dir lines carry rolled-up child IDs, so the root ID is genuinely unknowable until the last subtree resolves, validating the streaming premise). v8 buffering: cmd/c4/id.go:162/225 (outputManifest called once after scan), c4m/encoder.go:47-50 (Encode does m.Copy() + SortEntries — a full second copy).

findings.claim: The chain shape's core algebra works TODAY: a base section with null dir IDs/sizes plus ONE refinement patch of dir-only lines resolves through ApplyPatch to a manifest whose ComputeC4ID exactly equals the original full scan's root ID. Refinement can never be misread as removal, because removal requires an exactly-identical line and base dir lines (null ID) always differ from refined lines (non-nil ID).
findings.evidence: Empirical: constructed chain from real ModeFull scan; c4m.Unmarshal(chain-without-trailing-ID) → 7 entries, resolved ComputeC4ID == rootID true; DecodePatchChain+ResolvePatchChain likewise, dir entries refined (sub/ size 404, real ID). Code: c4m/operations.go:189-213 (ApplyPatch), :247-271 (clobber + recurse for dirs), :257-260 with :275-285 (removal only on entriesIdentical, which compares C4ID — nil vs non-nil always differs).

findings.claim: The proposal's signature guarantee — 'the LAST LINE of the stream is always the root ID' — is NOT expressible with today's decoders: a trailing bare root-ID line after the refinement patch makes strict Decode fail with 'empty patch section (at end of input)' in ALL FOUR implementations (Go, Python, TypeScript, Swift). Even flat text + trailing root ID fails. Only Go's DecodePatchChain tolerates it (drops it silently as an unverified 'validator'). Shipping Count 2/3 as specified requires coordinated decoder amendments across the suite.
findings.evidence: Go: c4m/decoder.go:124-132 (EOF flush: patchMode && empty section → ErrEmptyPatch); empirically reproduced: 'Decode ERROR: c4m: empty patch section (at end of input)' for both chain+trailing and flat+trailing. Python: c4py/src/c4py/decoder.py:166-167 (raise ValueError('empty patch section (at end of input)')). TypeScript: c4ts/packages/core/src/decoder.ts:468-470 (throw new EmptyPatchError('at end of input')). Swift: c4m-swift/Sources/C4M/Decoder.swift:105-107 (throw C4MError.emptyPatch). Tolerant path: c4m/chain.go:92-98 ('trailing bare C4 ID... is a validator, not a new section' — flushed only if entries exist).

(base) 5 files, 2 dirs / 2 ... +0 -0 ~2'; c4 split after.c4m contains boundary+patch but no closing ID; c4 id chain_trailing.c4m → 'Error loading ... empty patch section (at end of input)', exit=1; c4 id - < chain_trailing.c4m → full resolved listing, exit=0). findings.claim: Bare-ID boundary lines (including the final root ID) are never verified by any decode path — the doc comment claiming subsequent bare IDs 'must match the canonical C4 ID of all content above' is not enforced. A bogus 90-char boundary decodes without error. Therefore the streamed final root-ID line is an unverified assertion at read time; consumers wanting verification must recompute (as c4 patch/log do).
findings.evidence: c4m/decoder.go:34-35 (doc claims 'must match') vs decoder.go:99-101 (code comment: 'the bare ID is the previous block's identity (O(1), no accumulated state check)'); c4m/chain.go:92-94 (trailing ID dropped unverified). Relevant to Count 2/3 claim semantics: 'verification over assertion' pin means tail -1 scraping yields an ID the format itself does not validate.

findings.claim: For the chain-shape sub-question: per-directory patch sections are quadratic to decode and unusable at scale — one trailing patch is the only viable default. Measured: 20,400 entries, 400 per-dir sections took 16.59s to Unmarshal vs 102ms for the identical content as one trailing patch (163x); both resolve to equal IDs. Cause: Decode calls ApplyPatch at every boundary and ApplyPatch rebuilds full base+patch trees and reflattens each time (O(N) per section, O(N·D) total).
findings.evidence: Empirical scratch benchmark (perf/main.go): 'variant A (1 trailing patch): decode 101.6ms; variant B (400 per-dir patches): decode 16.59s; ratio 163.2x; ids equal: true'. Code: c4m/decoder.go:96-99 (ApplyPatch per boundary), c4m/operations.go:190-199 (buildPatchTree over entire base each call + flatten + SortEntries).

findings.claim: -e (aligned/ergonomic) output cannot stream: pretty encoding requires two global passes before the first byte — max size (comma-formatted width) over all entries and the C4-ID column derived from the global max line length (column starts at 80, grows in steps of 10, so one long name late in the tree shifts the ID column of every line). Encoder.Encode also unconditionally copies and sorts the whole manifest. '-e implies buffered' is the only option that adds no new concept; the aligned form remains chain-compatible on read since the decoder already skips space runs.

Decoder aligned-form tolerance: c4m/decoder.go:550-556 (lookahead skips whole space runs). CLI wiring: cmd/c4/id.go:729-735 (outputManifest → SetPretty).

findings.claim: Latent semantic footgun for any future incremental/streamed chain writing: in patch sections an exactly-duplicated line means REMOVAL, so a naive 'checkpoint' section that re-emits unchanged entries would delete them on resolve. The proposed refinement patch never trips this (null-ID base vs non-nil refined always differ), but any pinned chain-stream contract must state that patch sections carry only changed/refined lines.

Every ported decoder implements this rejection. The case file's constraint claim that 'bare-ID boundary lines are existing grammar' is true only for NON-trailing positions.

A bare C4 ID followed by nothing (EOF) ... is rejected as ErrEmptyPatch'); c4m/C4M-STANDARD.md:903/1015 (14.1 error table: 'Empty patch section | ErrEmptyPatch'); c4m/decoder.go:124-131 (Decode EOF flush returns ErrEmptyPatch); test pinning the behavior: c4m/patch_format_test.go:294-320 (TestDecodeEmptyPatchAtEOF). A streaming emitter must therefore produce exactly-canonical accumulated-state checkpoint IDs or verifying consumers reject valid output.

findings.claim: W1 (-s, kill mid-stream): the proposal converts v8's structurally-impossible crash exposure into a real one. Under v8-as-built, kill -9 mid-`-s` prints nothing (barrier and journal complete inside scanDirectory before the single fmt.Println; verified by 40 kills). Under streaming, a killed `-s` leaves child entry IDs on stdout that are not fetchable: during ingest every object sits at an `.ingest.*` staging name and is renamed to its hash name only inside the batch-barrier Sync, so a consumer who scraped a child ID from captured stdout (a) cannot `c4 cat` it, and (b) after power loss the bytes may not exist anywhere. Wrong conclusions a stdout consumer can draw: 'this ID is in the store', 'this ID is durable', and — for a regex/tail scraper that ignores exit status — 'the last ID printed is THE project identity' (a child's ID: founding complaint 3's exact failure, re-armed in the crash path only). Exit-checking consumers are unaffected.

(b) The killed stream's null directory IDs are textually indistinguishable from v7's 'unreadable at scan time' partial-scan class, conflating 'not yet refined' with 'permission-denied'. findings.claim: W2 (kill between last entry and refinement patch): the output is one valid c4m section with every file ID real and every directory ID/size null. This window genuinely vindicates 'partial data is data': the root ID is recomputable from the text alone (child file IDs are all present; directory IDs derive bottom-up), so `<killed-output> | c4 id -q -` yields THE correct root ID. The trap is that under -s this recomputed ID is not a claim: the journal has no entry, and listings/objects may still be unrenamed staging temps — recompute-then-assume-durable is the wrong conclusion; recompute-then-cat fails loudly. The pinned rule 'streamed lines are description, only the final bare line (and -q lines) carry printed⇒durable⇒recoverable' is sufficient for this window IF consumers are told claims are only assessable at process exit.

findings.claim: W3 (kill between refinement patch and final ID line) exposes a forced sub-decision the proposal leaves open, and one of its two resolutions silently resurrects the founding trap. The frozen chain grammar requires a bare ID line to introduce the refinement patch section (a bare ID after entries flushes the section and opens a new one based at that ID; EncodePatch writes exactly this shape). So a completed single-path stream contains TWO bare ID lines: the section boundary and the final root ID. If the boundary line is the ROOT ID (known at walk completion), then a kill in W3a (patch printed, barrier/journal not yet run) leaves stdout whose last bare ID line IS the root ID, unjournaled and possibly non-durable — a consumer applying 'the last bare line is the claim' forges a claim that dangles, silently. If the boundary is the UN-REFINED base section's own ID, a crash-scraped boundary ID is falsifiable in one command (cat fails; c4 cat -r | c4 id -q - mismatches) — loud, consistent with verification-over-assertion. Required pins: (1) the boundary ID is the base section's ID and must never equal the root ID; (2) a bare ID line is a claim only when it is the FINAL line of a stream whose process exited 0, or any -q line — claims are assessable only at exit. W3b (journal appended, final line unprinted) is exactly v7's documented in-between case and survives verbatim: c4 log holds the claim.

findings.claim: W4 (stdout write failure mid-stream): under streaming, an early-closing downstream reader KILLS the snapshot unless explicitly handled — in exactly the pipelines the proposal exists to enable. The Go runtime raises SIGPIPE (default disposition: process death) on EPIPE writes to fd 1, and the as-built code discards every stdout write error, so `c4 id -s dir | head -20` (or grep -m1, or a crashed consumer) would terminate c4 mid-ingest: no barrier, no journal entry, no error message — the verb invoked for its side effect silently did not happen. Under v8 this window is a few milliseconds post-barrier (the only -s stdout write follows the journal append, so the claim survives pipe death); under streaming it spans the whole scan. v7's pin 'a stdout write failure never rolls back store work' is insufficient — rollback is not the failure mode; cancellation is. Required pin: under -s, stdout death never cancels the snapshot — SIGPIPE handled, ingest+barrier+journal run to completion, exit 1, c4 log holds the ID (read-only id may simply abort, exit 1: it has no side effects; the two behaviors must be split explicitly).

findings.claim: Multi-path `-s a b c`: per-path claims and streamed listings CANNOT compose without ambiguity inside the frozen grammar — the proposal forces -q for multi-path. (1) Concatenation is semantic garbage: path a's trailing root-ID line followed by path b's entries is decoded as a patch section based at root(a), so the combined stdout resolves to 'b applied as edits to a'; the frozen grammar has no document separator and the case file forbids new syntax. (2) v7's multi-path pin 'a failed path prints no stdout line' is unsatisfiable under streaming — a path failing mid-scan has already streamed description. (3) Even at exit 0 a machine cannot split the stream: 'bare ID then entries' is exactly the shape of a refinement section, so per-path segment boundaries are undecidable. The exit-pairing rule remains coherent ONLY under -q, where it survives verbatim. Ruling options: refuse multi-path -s without -q with a teaching error (cleanest; matches 'one path, one line, one exit'), or have multiple paths imply -q; permitting interleaved multi-path streams as 'human-only output' would put un-parseable data on stdout, violating the stdout-is-data pin.

findings.claim: Torn-tail hazard: 'a killed scan leaves a valid partial description' (case file, Count 2) is not guaranteed — a kill can tear the final stdout line at a write boundary, and a torn entry line can parse SUCCESSFULLY as a WRONG entry, because the decoder treats the trailing C4 ID as optional and a name truncated mid-way is a valid shorter name (e.g. '- - 1234 parser.go c4…' torn after 'pars' parses as a file named 'pars' with null ID). So a killed stream can be silently corrupt at the tail, not merely incomplete. Required pins: the emitter writes each line in a single write(2) (no bufio flush mid-line; lines are far below PIPE_BUF), and the consumer rule 'discard a final line not terminated by a newline' is stated wherever killed-stream recovery is described.

(a) help first screen 'SNAP=$(c4 id -s dir/)  THE snapshot ID: one line, nothing else' → 'SNAP=$(c4 id -s -q dir/)  THE snapshot ID: one line, nothing else, printed only after the claim is durable'. (b) 'A snapshot ID prints only after everything it stored is on stable media — … a printed ID never dangles: if it printed, you can get it back' → 'THE snapshot ID — every -q line, and the final bare ID line of an -s stream that exits 0 — prints only after everything it names is on stable media: kill -9, panic, and power loss are one case, and a printed ID LINE never dangles — if the ID line printed, you can get it back. Every line above it is description, never a claim: an ID inside entry text promises nothing about the store, and a killed stream claims nothing.' (c) id(1) '-s: stdout is one line per path that succeeded… a failed path prints no stdout line' → 'With -s, stdout streams each path's description and ends it with that path's snapshot ID on a bare line, printed only after that path's claim is durable; with -q, one bare ID line per path that succeeded. A path failing mid-scan has already streamed description, so several paths compose only under -q: multi-path -s without -q is refused — one path, or -q.' (d) Exit map '1 error — lines already printed remain true claims' → '1 error — bare -q ID lines already printed remain true claims; streamed description lines were never claims.' (e) draft-v7 §3 'printed ⇒ fully durable… a printed ID never dangles' → 'a printed CLAIM never dangles — claims are exactly the -q lines and the final bare root-ID line of a completed -s stream; description lines are never claims and may name bytes never barriered.' (g) tail -1 is sanctioned only exit-conditioned: 'ID=$(c4 id dir/ | tail -1) is correct only after checking exit 0; the blessed capture remains -q.'

findings.claim: Net severity judgment on Count 3: ADOPTABLE WITH MODIFICATIONS — nothing fatal, but the proposal as written is not shippable. The honest cost, which the ruling must state rather than paper over: v8's strongest sentence — '-s stdout contains nothing but claims', which made even a negligent (exit-ignoring, regex-scraping) consumer crash-safe by construction — becomes a documentation rule ('the claim is the final line, on exit 0'), protecting only disciplined consumers. In exchange, the SUCCESS path improves (tail -1 correct, ls-l ergonomics, grep-during-scan, incremental partial capture), and the founding-complaint-3 consumer failed on a SUCCESSFUL run, which both v8 and v9 fix; the residual exposure class (ignores exit status AND consumes a crashed run's stdout) is narrow but real, and v8 had closed it structurally. Mandatory modifications for adoption: (1) exit-conditioned claim-line definition; (2) boundary ID = un-refined base-section ID, never the root; (3) multi-path -s forces -q (refuse otherwise); (4) SIGPIPE handling — -s completes its claim despite stdout death, exit 1; (5) line-atomic writes + discard-unterminated-final-line consumer rule; (6) readers verify a trailing boundary ID against the resolved manifest (today it is dropped unchecked); (7) streaming kill-crucible modes pass before freeze.

findings.claim: The proposed output shape — chain ending with a closing bare root-ID line — is REJECTED today by the workhorse decoder with 'c4m: empty patch section (at end of input)': reproduced by appending the root ID to a flat listing and running `c4 id chain.c4m` (exit 1), while the SAME bytes on stdin resolve fine via `c4 id -` (exit 0), because stdin tries DecodePatchChain first and file args use Decoder.Decode. Shipping the shape requires a coordinated decoder amendment across ≥4 implementations before v1.1.0, or the chain must not carry a trailing validator after the patch section — in which case tail -1's target is the patch section's opening boundary, not a guaranteed final line.

findings.claim: Multi-path `c4 id a b` under streaming is structurally incoherent, and tail -1 lies there: concatenating two per-path chains yields ONE chain in which path b's entries decode as a PATCH applied to path a (any bare-ID line starts a new section on the preceding base), so the redirected file resolves to a merged corruption while tail -1 returns only the last path's root. There is also no working precedent to preserve: v8-as-built multi-path non-quiet prints ONLY the first directory's manifest and exits 0, silently ignoring later paths (early `return` after the first dir/.c4m arg) — reproduced. Only -q's one-line-per-succeeded-path form is coherent multi-path. Pin required: -s/streaming forms either refuse multiple paths or document the concatenation as N independent claims that must never be redirected into one file.

findings.claim: A killed or failed scan mid-stream converts v8's fail-EMPTY into fail-PLAUSIBLE, and the shell hides the exit code from exactly the founding consumer profile: with no final line emitted, tail -1 returns an entry line or — worse — the mid-chain boundary bare ID (a well-formed 90-char ID that names an intermediate, never-claimed description), and in `VAR=$(c4 id -s dir | tail -1)` the pipeline returns tail's exit status, masking c4's failure. Under v8's '-s implies -q' + print barrier, a crashed snapshot printed NOTHING (buffered, barrier-gated), so capture was empty and failure loud. This is the one form where reverting '-s implies -q' measurably reopens the founding trap; it is bounded (requires crash + no exit discipline) but it is precisely the cold-scraper profile of complaint 3.

findings.claim: The streamed chain necessarily contains at least TWO bare-ID lines, only the last of which is the root: the chain grammar requires a boundary bare-ID line to open the refinement-patch section (without it the patch entries silently continue the base section), so 'the bare-ID line is the ID' — the v8 mental model — becomes ambiguous. A first-match scraper, or a consumer whose stream was cut between the mid-boundary and the closing line, captures the mid-boundary ID: a plausible, wrong, never-claimed identity. Per-directory patches (the Count 2 sub-question variant) multiply these decoy lines. The contract can only sanction 'the LAST line on exit 0/2', never 'the bare line'.

The unreadable-directory path must be fixed to record-nulls-and-continue before the final-line contract can hold on exit 2.

findings.claim: Net verdict on reverting '-s implies -q' (question 2): the reopening is real but bounded and one-sided. The founding scraper took the LAST regex match ('shipped the last leaf's ID') — under the streamed chain the last match is the closing root line, so that exact behavior becomes CORRECT on directory scans; first-match scrapers and crash-path captures regress versus v8 (findings 4-5); legacy `SNAP=$(c4 id -s dir/)` captures a multi-line var whose downstream use (restore target, cat) fails LOUDLY, not silently. Given -q is retained as the byte-pure form, the residual silent-wrong classes all require crash timing or exotic scraping plus ignored exit codes. Acceptable only with pins: the SCRIPTING block blesses exactly `SNAP=$(c4 id -s -q dir/)`; the final line is a claim only on exit 0/2; tail -1 is tolerated in prose, never printed as a contract line; -s multi-path restricted or documented non-redirectable (finding 3); and every -s form (dir, file, .c4m, stdin) must end stdout with the claimed ID line — today file/.c4m/stdin -s forms print the ID only via the implied -q, so an unpinned revert would leave `c4 id -s file.c4m` with NO claim on stdout at all.

findings.claim: With FULL as default (Count 1), the contract line becomes `CID=$(c4 id -q -m c dir/)` — and a two-flag content ID is an acceptable contract, not a trap: (a) two-flag contract lines are already frozen v7 precedent (`c4 id -q -m f proj/` appears in restore's OUTPUT text and EXAMPLES); (b) -q already composes with -m via the ID-bearing-level gate, which fails loudly for -m s/m; (c) the coherence win is real in code — the snapshot ID IS ComputeC4ID of the full manifest (storeManifestSelf stores canonical text whose hash is the root ID), so `c4 id -q dir/` at full default equals the -s snapshot ID on an unchanged tree, closing the v8 incoherence where the front-door -q ID could never match any journaled claim. Two residues to document, both safe-direction: (i) file/dir asymmetry — a file's -q is its content ID at every level ('its two IDs coincide'), so users who learn '-q = content ID' on files mis-generalize to directories, where bare -q now yields the machine-dependent full ID; (ii) T3 cross-machine comparison with bare -q yields false-DIFFERENT (mtimes), never false-same — annoying, not corrupting. Note the scope honestly: Count 1 reverses D1's default-placement sentence ('the default level for c4 id'), not the frozen 2026-07-09 full-null projection itself.

findings.claim: Count 4, trust-vs-scope on -c: no current documented workflow needs the retired filter semantics, and trust-only is the correct ruling. The retired semantics (scan-filter-continue: structure scan → hand-edit → hash only survivors; plus structure→metadata→full mode upgrades) was introduced by commit 62adeeb and documented in pre-v8 cli-reference.md ('Continue from Existing c4m', 'Removing entries'); the v8 docs sweep (2d71edd) purged it, and today's docs route scan-time cost exclusively to --exclude ('When to exclude at scan time vs filter after' now names only --exclude) while every recipe filters AFTER scanning as text. The old doc itself conceded --exclude 'is simpler for known patterns'. --exclude does NOT cover three residues, none appearing in any doc or recipe: keep-set inversion (must generate the complement as exclude patterns), filenames containing glob metacharacters (patterns are byte-exact globs with no documented escape), and progressive upgrade of one description's knowledge level. Against overloading: the blessed fast re-snapshot `c4 id -s -c prior.c4m proj/` would, under filter semantics, silently OMIT every file created since the guide — a data-loss-shaped silent wrong snapshot; and the 'null-ID guide entries imply filter' variant is doubly poisoned — it collides with Count 1's nulls-mean-ignorance, and a guide produced by a partial scan (unreadable file recorded with null ID, exit 2) would silently convert that recorded ignorance into a filter on the next re-scan. One cleanup owed either way: the dormant filter implementation scan.WithGuide ('Only entries present in the guide will be included… enables the scan-filter-continue workflow') still ships in the library beside WithReuseGuide — two guide concepts, one idea; delete or quarantine it per the one-implementation-per-idea pin.
